correctness.rationale: Global distance is established by sector development, with all winding competitors of developed angular lift at least pi bounded below by r+s. Eccentricity reduces to apex and antipodal rim distances, yielding exhaustive piecewise optimization and equality-locus proof. Uniform lateral area integration gives a strict radial quadratic; monotone sinc/tangent quotients give exactly two intersections. Product-radial convexity proves diameter and sharp ratio. Actual standalone program passed 2,857,130 counted finite checks across 66 cone ratios; finite checks do not replace infinite proof.

evidence: Ahn et al., A linear-time algorithm for the geodesic center of a simple polygon (2015): geodesic center on a polygonal **planar domain**, not a cone lateral quotient.
Aronov et al., Facility Location on Terrains (2001 report): facility-location problems for specified finite sets of sites, not whole lateral surfaces and no analytic cone-parameter classification.
MathOverflow geodesic poles question and answer identify geodesic radius versus mean-distance functionals but do not give a cone-center theorem.
broader_coverage.reasoning: These results concern either different metric spaces, finite site sets, or different objectives. Neither implies the continuous all-target Chebyshev formula, area squared-distance minimizers and their two coincidences.

originality.rationale: The examined full or materially relevant primary sources supply cone unfolding, center algorithms for planar polygon domains, or finite-site terrain location, but not the simultaneous all-cone minimax and uniform-area Fréchet center loci, their exactly two coincidence cone angles, and the sharp family-specific radius/diameter theorem. Prior cone pairwise-distance energy and frustum diameter results do not imply the optimizer sets. Historical-priority uncertainty remains for unindexed specialized sources.
residual_risks: An unindexed older computation of the minimax center of a finite circular cone might give some or all Chebyshev branches.
The 2001 terrain facility-location PDF was only partly inspected, and the interactive 2010 cone demonstration notebook itself was not read; neither accessible material establishes the exact claim.
Coincidence angles and the Fréchet optimizer could have appeared in specialized metric-measure cone literature not retrieved by semantic searching.
Negative database searches do not prove absolute novelty; independent expert priority review is not performed.

value.rationale: Chebyshev minimax center and intrinsic area Fréchet center are fundamental metric-center functionals. Their complete optimizer loci on the canonical cone family, topological transition from center circle to apex, exactly two isolated coincidences and sharp covering-radius/diameter inequality provide structurally motivated classification for an entire continuously varying geometric family. This goes beyond deriving one obvious distance integral or an arbitrary finite table.
